images.caption:
This Photo was taken in Philippine national Museum
Context: 
"Church Architecture of Cebu"

Church architecture was a necessity for the evangelization of the Filipino people during Spanish colonial rule. Churches also served political and practical purposes that furthered the development of communities. Before the arrival of the Spaniards, Filipino natives used light construction materials; early churches were designed the same way until innovations led to the use of stone and masonry to create more long-lasting structures. Cebu's history can be traced to the founding of the Basilica Minore del Santo Niño de Cebu, which legend says was the site where an image of the Holy Child was discovered, and Miguel Lopez de Legazpi established the first Spanish settlement in the area of the discovery soon after.

images.caption: Planning any Spanish colonial-era settlement emphasized defense, particularly to scare off Moro raiders and other dangers. When stone constructions of churches became typical, it was then able to be used as defensible structures, with their prime location, large scale, and prominence The Church of Our Lady of Patrocinio in Boljoon, Cebu, is a fine example of a church used as a defensive structure. Constructed in 1599, the fortress church is on a hill overlookıng the sea, allowing it to give early warning against Moro raiders The church also features bell towers that were used as watchtowers and overall presents an austere, unadorned architectural volume and exterior constructed of locally quarried coral stone topped with a roof of terracotta tiles
